title: Generative Interactions: Weaving Multiparty Human Motion with Bilevel Latent Dynamics
abstract: arXiv:2609.37708v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human social behaviour is not a collection of independent motions, but a jointly organised process in which group dynamics and individual variation continuously shape one another. Yet existing social motion models often prioritise plausible trajectories while leaving interaction state implicit, limiting their ability to transfer across groups, tasks, and partial-observation regimes. To address this gap, we introduce Bilevel Representations for Agent Interaction Dynamics (BRAID), a hierarchical sequential latent-variable model for generative multi-person interaction. BRAID explicitly formulates social motion generation as a meta-transfer learning problem: shared interaction priors are learned across datasets and adapted through arbitrary context sets of observed people and joints. translated_title: 生成式交互：基于双层潜在动态的多方人体运动编织
translated_abstract: 人类社会行为并非独立运动的集合，而是一个共同组织的过程，其中群体动态与个体差异持续地相互塑造。然而，现有的社会运动模型往往侧重于生成合理的轨迹，而将交互状态保持为隐式形式，这限制了模型在跨群体、跨任务以及部分可观测场景下的迁移能力。为解决这一缺口，我们提出了面向智能体交互动态的双层表示模型（BRAID），这是一种用于生成式多人交互的分层序列潜变量模型。BRAID明确地将社会运动生成形式化为一个元迁移学习问题：共享的交互先验在多个数据集上学习，并通过由任意数量观测人物及关节构成的上下文集合进行自适应调整。该模型通过捕捉共享交互动态的群体级潜在状态和捕捉个体差异的人物级潜在状态来刻画每个场景，……
tldr: 提出BRAID——一种分层序列潜变量模型，将多人社会运动生成形式化为元迁移学习问题，通过群体级与人物级双层潜在状态显式建模社会交互，从而实现跨群体、跨任务及部分可观测场景的迁移能力。
en_tdlr: BRAID, a hierarchical sequential latent-variable model, formulates generative multiparty social motion as a meta-transfer learning problem, explicitly modeling interactions via group-level and person-level latent states to enable transfer across groups, tasks, and partial-observation regimes.
